articles.summary: Nvidia's board of directors "isn't considering" having Jensen Huang return as CEO, according to a report from CNBC. A source tells the outlet the board "is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back." articles.title: Google Maps can now create trip itineraries for you
articles.summary: Google is launching a new AI trip-planning feature for Maps that allows the app to create custom itineraries for you and provide real-time details about each stop. The update, which is rolling out to the Gemini-powered Ask Maps chatbot inside the app, lets you plan a one-day outing or a trip spanning several days. As […]

articles.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
articles.summary: Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.

articles.title: Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
articles.summary: Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary: Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.

articles.title: Scientists overcome a hidden obstacle to more powerful quantum computers
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a way to operate multiple silicon qubits simultaneously with remarkable accuracy, overcoming a major challenge in scaling up quantum computers. Their new technique maintained accuracy of approximately 99.9% even when all five qubits were running at once, opening the door to larger and more powerful quantum processors.

articles.title: FBI says Artex AI open source hacking tool used to breach networks in ‘under three hours’
articles.summary: The FBI says that the open source hacking tool was used in cyberattacks targeting a U.S. IT giant and the South Korean financial industry.

articles.title: Jordan Belfort’s new AI voice startup, Tone, wants to sell like the ‘Wolf of Wall Street’
articles.summary: Belfort claims his AI sales voice can already close deals almost as well as the best human salespeople, and he thinks it will catch up in a year.

articles.title: Audible turns to AI to help users discover audiobooks
articles.summary: Audible's new AI-generated audio previews summarize a book's themes and what readers liked about it, in addition to playing the narrated sample.

articles.title: Anthropic's IPO: How do you price the future of AI?
articles.summary: Speculation over Anthropic's stock market valuation has highlighted one of the riskiest bets in finance: trying to put a price on the future of artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
articles.summary: Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang's reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO. articles.title: Sam Altman says he wants everyone ‘to have a lot of RAM’
articles.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is once again addressing his controversial comments on PC RAM purchases. "I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM, I think everybody should be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer," Altman said today. "I think the home tinkering is great." […]

articles.title: Big Nuclear isn’t worried about the Democrats stopping data centers
articles.summary: Constellation Energy - America's largest operator of nuclear power plants - does not share Wall Street's concerns that the Democrats will slow down data center development. On the company's third-quarter earnings call last week, CEO Joe Dominguez was, for lack of a better word, unbothered as he addressed the blue wave. "I do think we've […]

articles.title: US data centers now burn more electricity than a midsized country
articles.summary: Fossil fuels are still the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, a new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability shows. They likely burn through more electricity collectively than many countries do, resulting in a serious amount of greenhouse gas emissions. The study homes in on hyperscale facilities - the […]

articles.title: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
articles.summary: Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors. Basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on […]

articles.title: Audible is trying to make it easier to find audiobooks you’ll actually like
articles.summary: Audible is introducing an AI-assisted synopsis feature that's designed to help users determine whether they'll enjoy an audiobook before they jump in and start listening to it. The new audio discovery feature combines audiobook samples, AI overviews, and author commentary to give users more information before choosing their next story, in addition to recommended audiobook […]

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.

articles.title: Tiny magnetic vortices could help computers work more like your brain
articles.summary: Scientists have filmed tiny magnetic vortices called skyrmions melting out of an organized lattice for the first time, revealing new ways to manipulate these unusual structures. The breakthrough could help make brain-like computers a reality, potentially enabling dramatically smaller and more energy-efficient technology.

articles.title: Researchers develop AI-powered, human-centered framework for supplier selection
articles.summary: With global supply chains facing increasingly complex and unpredictable socio-economic, environmental and regulatory conditions, many companies are facing a growing need for quick and effective supplier evaluation. To address this concern, a group of researchers at Constructor University have proposed a new supplier selection framework that combines the interpretive power of large language model (LLM) AI with human oversight to improve supplier outcomes.

articles.title: Apple faces French trial over alleged planned obsolescence of iPhones: Source
articles.summary: Apple will stand trial in Paris in June 2027 on suspicion of having organized the planned obsolescence of several iPhone models by preventing repairs outside official outlets, a source close to the case told AFP on Tuesday.

articles.title: Singapore seeks 'trusted access' to AI chips after US curbs
articles.summary: Singapore said Tuesday it was in talks with the United States to ensure access to advanced AI chips after Washington imposed curbs on overseas data centers meant to block Chinese firms from the technology.

articles.title: From flipping its pages to sitting on it, the phone book infiltrated American life—then vanished
articles.summary: The telephone book started as a one-page list of 50 telephone subscribers in 1878 in New Haven, Connecticut. It was later, in the late 1900s, when it became the utilitarian device that was ever-present in my household.

articles.title: Florida's stormwater ponds become floating solar farms as costs fall and demand rises
articles.summary: Of the tens of thousands of retention ponds designed to collect runoff during Florida's frequent downpours, some are also being used to generate solar power, expanding sustainable energy production in the Sunshine State.

articles.title: Head of China's Baidu warns of AI 'bubble' ahead of APEC talks
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence adoption is not boosting profits for most companies, the head of Chinese internet giant Baidu said Tuesday, ahead of talks between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping expected to address the risks posed by the sensitive technology.

articles.title: United Airlines says it resolved a technology issue that affected departing flights
articles.summary: United Airlines said Monday that it had resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, just days after a malfunction in the Federal Aviation Administration's network prompted a nationwide ground stop.

articles.title: A technical issue at JPMorgan Chase triggers online banking delays for major US banks
articles.summary: Thousands of customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major U.S. banks and the money transfer service Zelle on Monday after a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system.

articles.title: Chat-based AI lets users run complex alloy calculations on their own computers
articles.summary: Computational materials science develops models and simulations that are indispensable for the development of complex materials, such as high-entropy alloys. Researchers at Empa in Thun have developed an AI framework that allows researchers to operate these complex tools via a simple text chat—a kind of ChatGPT for materials but grounded in scientific knowledge and calculated on-demand on the user's own computer.
